newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Arafat says Netanyahu doesn't want peace.
newsitem.headline: Arafat says Netanyahu doesn't want peace.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat said on Tuesday that Benjamin Netanyahu's insistence on building Jewish settlements meant the Israeli prime minister did not want peace.
Asked about Netanyahu's reassertion in Washington that he planned to go on building for settlers, Arafat told reporters in the Gaza Strip: "This means that he does not want peace."
U.S. President Bill Clinton failed to win concessions from Netanyahu to salvage Israeli-PLO peacemaking, marred by violence since Israel broke ground on a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.
Speaking on his return from a visit to India, Arafat rejected Netanyahu's accusations the Palestinian side was violating peace deals and said the PLO was committed to the agreements.
"He (Netanyahu) has to remember that we are completely committed to the peace process and that he has to be committed to it like us," Arafat said.
